implementation_notes: ActiveRecord ships the single-table mapper: subclassing a model whose table has a `type` column makes the library persist the class name and return the right subclass from any base-class query, so the mapper hierarchy is the model hierarchy itself and the column can be renamed via Base.inheritance_column. That is single table inheritance only - ActiveRecord has no class-table mapping - so a class-table shape is either hand-written per subclass (own table plus a belongs_to to the base) or delegated to Sequel's class_table_inheritance plugin.
code_sketch:
class Payment < ApplicationRecord; end
class CreditCardPayment < Payment; end   # stored with type = "CreditCardPayment"

Payment.create!(name: "x")               # type = "Payment"
CreditCardPayment.first                   # AR instantiates the subclass from the type column
# class-table shape: no AR support -> belongs_to to the base table, or Sequel:
# Payment.plugin :class_table_inheritance, key: :kind, table_map: {...}
pitfalls: The type column is an ordinary attribute: every new subclass instance starts dirty with type set, which surprises validations and change-tracking that compare changed attributes.
Discriminator values are class names by default, so renaming or namespacing a class orphans existing rows unless type values are mapped explicitly.
STI keeps every subclass column in one table, so NOT NULL constraints on subclass columns cannot be expressed; and deleting a subclass leaves orphan type values behind.

variants.name: Sequel class_table_inheritance plugin
variants.implementation_notes: Sequel's class_table_inheritance plugin is the class-table mapper: a root table holds the sti key column, each subclass that adds columns lives in its own table keyed by the same primary key, and datasets for a subclass select from a joined subquery so instances come back fully loaded; superclass queries return subclass instances and load the subclass columns lazily (via the lazy_attributes plugin it requires). Choose it when the schema already has per-class tables and the duplicated base columns of STI are not acceptable.
pitfalls: Subclass datasets select from a subquery, so they cannot be updated, deleted or inserted into directly - deletes must go through each cti_table.
A subclass table must not repeat a superclass column name; the plugin does not support overlapping column names.
Superclass instances carry only root-table columns and cost one extra query per instance when a subclass column is first touched.
